reasoning: The mechanism reproduces and is real: server.py:1307-1315 stamps loadedAt = _utc_now_iso() on load, and both /api/metrics (:4671-4700) and /api/health (:4509-4520) derive age from it, as does the ops-alert call site (:11749-11762). Today the equality still holds byte-for-byte (571 == 571) and the demonstration is now sharper than the author's: the loaded snapshot's own sourceRunSummary.finishedAt makes the data 6.25h old, PAST the 6h stale threshold, while /api/health reports 0.2h and data_stale False — and /api/status.source_health independently reports 6.17h from the same process, so the honest number is three feet away exactly as claimed. StaleDataBanner is app-wide (AppShellWrapper.jsx:94) and reads data_age_hours with WARNING_HOURS=6, so the silence is real. Rescoped on two points the finding overstates. (1) 'They are numerically identical to uptime' is not a property of the metric, it is a property of the disk-cache-only state. server.py:2414 re-stamps loadedAt on every SUCCESSFUL scrape, so in normal production operation (2h cadence) loadedAt IS the scrape-completion time and the reported age is honest. The identity is permanent HERE only because the audit harness monkeypatches run_scraper to a no-op — that half of the evidence is harness-shaped. (2) 'A server that restarts on any cadence under 6h can never report stale data, however old it is' is wrong as stated: after one restart the age restarts from zero and still crosses 6h six hours later, so a single restart DELAYS the warning by the data's age at boot rather than suppressing it. Permanent suppression needs sub-6h restarts, which is not a normal cadence. What survives is a genuine monitoring blind spot — the staleness alarm is silenced by the very action an operator takes during a scrape outage, and the ops email inherits it — but nothing on any board shows a wrong VALUE, and the failure needs a compound precondition (scrape failing AND a restart). That is P2 on this audit's scale, not P1: P1 here implies a present-tense wrong number on a surface a user acts on, and this is a delayed warning. Not fixed at HEAD.

correctedBlastRadius.note: playersAffected 1092 is not meaningful — no player value is wrong, only the freshness warning is delayed. routes: /api/metrics, /api/health, and the ops_alerts leg of /api/signal-alerts/run. pages 41 is fair since StaleDataBanner renders in AppShellWrapper on every page, but the effect is an absent banner, not a wrong number.

whatWouldSettleIt: Restore the scraper on a scratch instance, let one scrape land, and re-read /api/metrics: if data_age_seconds diverges from uptime_seconds and tracks the scrape, the permanent-identity claim is confirmed as harness-only and the residual defect is exactly the restart-resets-the-clock window. A test asserting data_age != uptime after a cache load (the finding's own requiredRepair) would pin it.

reasoning: The core mechanism is confirmed: AppShell.jsx:33-75 gates the private data fetch on exactly one prefix list (PUBLIC_ONLY_ROUTE_PREFIXES = ['/league'], added for data-leak reasons), so PrivateAppShell calls useDynastyData() on every other route including board-less pages and Next's not-found — I re-measured a cold /news hard load and it does fetch /api/dynasty-data?view=array. Three parts of the finding do not survive re-measurement. (1) Attribution: 'decode 11.7-13.1 MB' is the sum of decodedBodySize over ALL resource entries (w26_probe.py:245), not the contract. The player contract is 6,515,205 b decoded / 671,811 b on the wire. Of the rest, 3,897,831 b decoded / 369,861 b wire is a SECOND request, POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta, and that one is conditional on the user having customized source weights (dynasty-data.js:2017-2035 — a default user takes the !customized branch and never posts it). The remaining ~1.3 MB decoded is app JS/CSS that any page must load. So the title's 'fetches the full multi-megabyte player contract' is right, but 'costs 12.5 MB' is not the contract's cost, and the numericProof's formula (whole-page decodedBytes minus rendered board = waste) charges the Next bundle to this defect. (2) 'On mobile this is the dominant cost of every navigation in the app' is false. AppShell lives in the root layout and does not remount on client-side navigation, and dynasty-data.js:1413-1440 adds a module-level cache with a 30s TTL plus in-flight dedupe. Measured: navigating /rankings -> /news by clicking the nav link produced exactly ONE /api/dynasty-data request in total. The original probe's per-page cost is an artifact of probing each route with a fresh page.goto. (3) The flagship example is a Next 404 (/terminal has no directory under frontend/app), so 'a mistyped URL costs 1.0 MB' is true of a cold context only, and ~0.67 MB of that is the contract. What is left is a real but ordinary perf inefficiency: a cold entry on a board-less page pays ~672 KB over the wire and a 6.5 MB JSON parse it does not use, to keep global search and the player popup working. No number a user acts on is wrong, ETag/304 revalidation and the module cache bound the repeat cost, and the finding itself credits both. P2, not P1.

correctedBlastRadius.note: routesAffected 1: only /api/dynasty-data is the shell fetch; /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta rides the same code path but is user-state-conditional. playersAffected is not a meaningful axis for a payload-size finding — the correct cost axis is 671,811 b wire / 6,515,205 b decoded per COLD load of a board-less page, and 0 additional bytes per in-session navigation.

whatWouldSettleIt: A cold-cache mobile trace of the first entry into the app (which is the one load that genuinely pays it) with the contract fetch isolated from the bundle, plus a measurement of the >30s-TTL revalidation path — if that returns 304 with a near-zero body, the per-navigation cost is confirmed as ~0 and the finding is strictly a first-paint cost.
